answer: When I think about business, one success story from my own country always comes to mind. A businessperson I really admire is the founder of a local company that started as a tiny shop and grew into a respected national brand. The business makes food products, things like biscuits and snacks that you can find in almost every corner shop in Bangladesh. What I find inspiring is not just the commercial success, but the way he treated his employees like family throughout. He was known for reinvesting profits into his staff and community rather than simply [[maximising]] his own wealth. In terms of what he achieved, I have read that he took real risks in the early years, when the venture could easily have [[collapsed]]. Over time, though, he turned a single shop into several factories, providing jobs for a great many people, including in rural areas where work is scarce. That kind of courage, combined with a clear [[vision]], is what separates genuine entrepreneurs from the rest. He also stayed grounded despite his success, which earned him enormous loyalty. As for why I admire him, it is partly personal, because my father ran a small business for over thirty years, so I know how hard it is simply to survive. What I admire most is that he proved you can build something profitable while remaining [[ethical]]. Honestly, in an age when many businesses cut corners, his example is refreshing, and it has shaped how I think about running a company myself one day.

followUps.q: Would you like to start your own business?
followUps.answer: Possibly, one day. With my background in business administration, it is tempting, but I would want some experience abroad first. Starting a company without proper preparation seems far too [[precarious]] to me.

followUps.q: Do you think successful businesspeople should give back to society?
followUps.answer: Yes, I do. Businesses depend on their communities, so it seems fair that they share some of their success, whether through charity, fair wages or supporting local education.

note: Added what the business makes, his achievements (shop to factories, no figures), a personal link to my father's small business and a clearer bullet order.
